units.zh: 梁書卷第三十 列傳第二十四
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 30, Biography 24
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 30, Biography 24

units.zh: 裴子野
units.en: Pei Ziye
units.literal: Pei Ziye

units.zh: 裴子野字幾原，河東聞喜人，晉太子左率康八世孫。
units.en: Pei Ziye, styled Jiyuan, came from Wenxi in Hedong and was the eighth-generation descendant of Pei Kang, who had served Jin as Left Commander of the Heirs Apparent.
units.literal: Pei Ziye, styled Jiyuan, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong, eighth-generation descendant of Pei Kang, Left Commander of the Heirs Apparent of Jin.

units.zh: 兄黎，弟楷、綽，並有盛名，所謂「四裴」也。
units.en: His elder brother Li and his younger brothers Kai and Chuo were all famous, and together they were known as the "Four Peis."
units.literal: His elder brother Li and younger brothers Kai and Chuo all enjoyed great renown — the so-called "Four Peis."

units.zh: 曾祖松之，宋太中大夫。
units.en: His great-grandfather Pei Songzhi had been a Grand Master of the Palace under the Song.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Songzhi was Grand Master of the Palace of Song.

units.zh: 祖駰，南中郎外兵參軍。
units.en: His grandfather Pei Yin had served as External Army Aide to the Southern Central Commandant.
units.literal: His grandfather Yin was an External Army Aide to the Southern Central Commandant.

units.zh: 父昭明，通直散騎常侍。
units.en: His father Pei Zhaoming had been Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry.
units.literal: His father Zhaoming was Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry.

units.zh: 子野生而偏孤，爲祖母所養，年九歲，祖母亡，泣血哀慟，家人異之。
units.en: Ziye lost his father early and was raised by his grandmother. When she died, he was only nine, yet he mourned her so bitterly that he wept blood; his family marveled at it.
units.literal: Ziye was born fatherless and was raised by his grandmother. At age nine, when his grandmother died, he wept blood in grief and mourning; his family found this extraordinary.

units.zh: 少好學，善屬文。
units.en: As a youth he loved study and was accomplished at writing.
units.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

units.zh: 起家齊武陵王國左常侍，右軍江夏王參軍，遭父憂去職。
units.en: He entered service under Qi as Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Prince Wuling and as an aide to the Prince of Jiangxia in the Right Army, then resigned when his father died.
units.literal: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Prince Wuling of Qi and as an aide to the Prince of Jiangxia in the Right Army, then left office upon his father's death.

units.zh: 居喪盡禮，每之墓所，哭泣處草爲之枯，有白兔馴擾其側。
units.en: He observed mourning to the letter. Each time he visited the grave, the grass withered beneath his weeping, and a white hare would come and linger tamely beside him.
units.literal: In mourning he observed every rite. Whenever he went to the grave, the grass withered where he wept, and a white hare would come tamely to linger at his side.

units.zh: 天監初，尚書僕射范雲嘉其行，將表奏之，會雲卒，不果。
units.en: Early in the Tianjian era, Vice Director of the Secretariat Fan Yun admired his conduct and was about to recommend him to the throne, but Yun died before he could carry it out.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tianjian era, Vice Director of the Secretariat Fan Yun praised his conduct and was about to memorialize the throne on his behalf, but Yun died before he could do so.

units.zh: 樂安任昉有盛名，爲後進所慕，遊其門者，昉必相薦達。
units.en: Ren Fang of Le'an was widely famous, and younger scholars looked up to him. He always recommended and advanced those who sought him out.
units.literal: Ren Fang of Le'an enjoyed great fame and was admired by younger men. Whoever came to his gate, Fang would recommend and advance.

units.zh: 子野於昉爲從中表，獨不至，昉亦恨焉。
units.en: Ziye was Fang's cousin on his mother's side, yet he alone never called on him, and Fang bore a grudge for it.
units.literal: Ziye was Fang's cousin on his mother's side, yet he alone did not visit; Fang resented this as well.

units.zh: 久之，除右軍安成王參軍，俄遷兼廷尉正。
units.en: After some time he was appointed aide to the Prince of Ancheng in the Right Army, and soon afterward was made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.
units.literal: After some time he was appointed aide to the Prince of Ancheng in the Right Army, and soon afterward was made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.

units.zh: 時三官通署獄牒，子野嘗不在，同僚輒署其名，奏有不允，子野從坐免職。
units.en: At that time the three bureaus jointly countersigned prison documents. Once when Ziye was away, a colleague signed his name in his place; when the memorial was rejected, Ziye was dismissed as an accomplice.
units.literal: At that time the three bureaus jointly signed prison documents. Once when Ziye was absent, a colleague signed his name for him; when the memorial was disapproved, Ziye was dismissed as an accomplice.

units.zh: 或勸言諸有司，可得無咎。
units.en: Some urged him to plead his case before the authorities so that he might escape punishment.
units.literal: Some urged him to plead his case before the authorities so that he might escape blame.

units.zh: 子野笑而答曰：「雖慚柳季之道，豈因訟以受服。」
units.en: Ziye smiled and replied, "Though I may fall short of Liu Ji's example, I would not put on mourning merely because of a lawsuit."
units.literal: Ziye smiled and replied, "Though I may fall short of Liu Ji's conduct, how could I put on mourning garb merely because of litigation?"

units.zh: 自此免黜久之，終無恨意。
units.en: From then on he remained out of office for a long time, yet he never bore a grudge.
units.literal: From then on he was dismissed for a long while, yet he harbored no resentment.

units.zh: 二年，吳平侯蕭景爲南兗州刺史，引爲冠軍錄事，府遷職解。
units.en: In the second year, Marquis of Wuping Xiao Jing became regional inspector of South Yanzhou and took Ziye on as recorder for the Champion General; when the headquarters was transferred, the appointment ended.
units.literal: In the second year, Marquis of Ping of Wu Xiao Jing became regional inspector of South Yanzhou and took him on as recorder for the Champion General; when the headquarters moved, the post was dissolved.

units.zh: 時中書范縝與子野未遇，聞其行業而善焉。
units.en: At that time Fan Zhen of the Secretariat had not yet met Ziye, but having heard of his conduct and accomplishments, he thought well of him.
units.literal: At that time Fan Zhen of the Secretariat and Ziye had not yet met, but having heard of his conduct and accomplishments, Zhen thought well of him.

units.zh: 會遷國子博士，乃上表讓之曰：「伏見前冠軍府錄事參軍河東裴子野，年四十，字幾原，幼稟至人之行，長厲國士之風。
units.en: When he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy, he submitted a memorial yielding the post to another, saying: "I have observed the former recorder of the Champion General's headquarters, Pei Ziye of Hedong, age forty, styled Jiyuan, who from youth embodied the conduct of a sage and in maturity cultivated the bearing of a true gentleman of the state.
units.literal: When he was transferred to be Erudite of the Imperial Academy, he submitted a memorial yielding the post, saying: "I have observed the former recorder of the Champion General's headquarters, Pei Ziye of Hedong, age forty, styled Jiyuan, who in youth received the conduct of a sage and in maturity cultivated the bearing of a state-worthy man.

units.zh: 居喪有禮，毀瘠幾滅，免憂之外，蔬水不進。
units.en: In mourning he observed every rite to the point of wasting away; even after the mourning period ended, he would take in neither vegetables nor water.
units.literal: In mourning he observed the rites; his emaciation nearly consumed him, and after the mourning period ended he would take in neither vegetables nor water.

units.zh: 棲遲下位，身賤名微，而性不憛憛，情無汲汲，是以有識嗟推，州閭嘆服。
units.en: He lingered in humble office, obscure and of little renown, yet his nature was never restless and his heart never grasping; men of discernment praised and recommended him, and his neighbors marveled at him.
units.literal: He lingered in low office, his person humble and his name obscure, yet his nature was not restless and his heart not grasping; therefore the discerning praised and pushed him forward, and his district sighed in admiration.

units.zh: 且家傳素業，世習儒史，苑囿經籍，遊息文藝。
units.en: His family has handed down its scholarly calling for generations, and he has long practiced Confucian learning and history, ranging through the classics and finding his recreation in literature and the arts.
units.literal: Moreover, his family has handed down its proper calling for generations, and he has long practiced Confucian learning and history, ranging through the classics and finding recreation in letters and the arts.

units.zh: 著《宋略》二十卷，彌綸首尾，勒成一代，屬辭比事，有足觀者。
units.en: He has written the Song Summary in twenty juan, spanning a whole age from beginning to end; in arranging words and comparing events, it is well worth reading.
units.literal: He has composed the Song Summary in twenty juan, spanning beginning to end and binding together a whole age; in arranging words and comparing events, there is much worth viewing.

units.zh: 且章句洽悉，訓故可傳。
units.en: His commentarial passages are thorough, and his glosses on ancient terms are fit to be handed down.
units.literal: Moreover, his commentarial passages are thorough and familiar, and his glosses on old terms can be handed down.

units.zh: 脫置之膠庠，以弘獎後進，庶一夔之辯可尋，三豕之疑無謬矣。
units.en: If he were placed in the Academy to encourage younger scholars, perhaps the discernment of a Kui might be found again and errors like the "three pigs" would never arise.
units.literal: If he were placed in the Academy to encourage and reward the rising generation, perhaps Kui's discernment could be sought again and the error of the three pigs would find no place.

units.zh: 伏惟皇家淳耀，多士盈庭，官人邁乎有媯，棫朴越於姬氏，苟片善宜錄，無論厚薄，一介可求，不由等級。
units.en: Your Majesty's house shines with pure brilliance, and talented men fill the court. Its officials surpass those of the age of Gui, and its supply of able men exceeds that of the Zhou. If even the slightest merit deserves record, without regard to high or low station, a single worthy man may be sought without regard to rank.
units.literal: Your Majesty's house shines with pure brilliance; talented men fill the court. Its officials surpass those of the House of Gui, and its timber for building exceeds that of the House of Ji. If even a fragment of merit should be recorded, regardless of depth or shallowness, a single man of worth may be sought without regard to rank.

units.zh: 臣歷觀古今人君，欽賢好善，未有聖朝孜孜若是之至也。
units.en: Your servant has surveyed rulers ancient and modern who honored the worthy and loved goodness, yet none has matched the diligence of this sacred court.
units.literal: Your servant has surveyed rulers ancient and modern who honored the worthy and loved goodness, yet none has reached the diligence of this sacred court.

units.zh: 敢緣斯義，輕陳愚瞽，乞以臣斯忝，回授子野。
units.en: Venturing on this principle, I humbly set forth my dull counsel and beg that the post your unworthy servant now holds may be transferred to Ziye.
units.literal: I venture on this principle lightly to set forth my dull blindness, begging that the post in which your servant is unworthy may be transferred to Ziye.

units.zh: 如此，則賢否之宜，各全其所，訊之物議，誰曰不允。
units.en: If it were so, the worthy and the unworthy would each occupy their proper place, and if one asked public opinion, who would call it unjust?
units.literal: If it were so, then the fitting place for worthy and unworthy would each be preserved, and if one asked public opinion, who would say it was not acceptable?

units.zh: 臣與子野雖未嘗銜杯，訪之邑裏，差非虛謬，不勝慺慺微見，冒昧陳聞。
units.en: Your servant and Ziye have never shared a cup together, yet inquiring in the district, what is said of him is not greatly exaggerated. Unable to restrain my earnest sincerity, I venture this slight view and presumptuously lay it before Your Majesty.
units.literal: Your servant and Ziye have never shared a cup, yet inquiring in the district, the report is not greatly false. Unable to restrain my earnest sincerity, I venture this slight view and presumptuously report it.

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀憐悾款，鑒其愚實，干犯之諐，乞垂赦宥。」
units.en: I bow my head and hope Your Majesty will pity my sincere earnestness, discern my foolish honesty, and extend pardon for this presumptuous offense."
units.literal: I bow my head and hope Your Majesty will pity my sincere earnestness, discern my foolish truthfulness, and extend pardon for this offense of presumption."

units.zh: 有司以資歷非次，弗爲通。
units.en: The relevant offices, holding that his qualifications were out of order, did not approve the request.
units.literal: The relevant offices, on the grounds that his qualifications were out of order, did not approve it.

units.zh: 尋除尚書比部郎，仁威記室參軍。
units.en: Soon afterward he was appointed Lang of the Comparison Bureau in the Secretariat and recorder for Prince Renwei.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Lang of the Comparison Bureau in the Secretariat and recorder for Prince Renwei.

units.zh: 出爲諸暨令，在縣不行鞭罰，民有爭者，示之以理，百姓稱悅，合境無訟。
units.en: He was sent out as magistrate of Zhuji. In the county he never used the lash or fines; when the people quarreled, he showed them reason, and they praised him with joy — throughout the whole district there were no lawsuits.
units.literal: He went out as magistrate of Zhuji. In the county he did not use the lash or fines; when the people had disputes, he showed them reason, and the common folk praised him with joy — throughout the whole district there were no lawsuits.

units.zh: 初，子野曾祖松之，宋元嘉中受詔續修何承天《宋史》，未及成而卒，子野常欲繼成先業。
units.en: Earlier, Ziye's great-grandfather Pei Songzhi, in the Yuanjia era of Song, had received an edict to continue He Chengtian's History of Song, but died before finishing it; Ziye had long wished to complete his ancestor's work.
units.literal: Earlier, Ziye's great-grandfather Songzhi, in the Yuanjia era of Song, received an edict to continue and revise He Chengtian's History of Song, but died before completing it; Ziye had long wished to carry on and finish his ancestor's work.

units.zh: 及齊永明末，沈約所撰《宋書》旣行，子野更刪撰爲《宋略》二十卷。
units.en: By the end of the Yongming era of Qi, Shen Yue's History of Song had already appeared; Ziye then abridged and rewrote it as the Song Summary in twenty juan.
units.literal: By the end of the Yongming era of Qi, Shen Yue's History of Song had already appeared; Ziye further abridged and composed it into the Song Summary in twenty juan.

units.zh: 其敘事評論多善，約見而歎曰：「吾弗逮也。」
units.en: Its narrative and commentary were largely excellent. When Shen Yue saw it he sighed and said, "I do not match him."
units.literal: Its narrative and commentary were largely excellent. When Yue saw it he sighed and said, "I do not match him."

units.zh: 蘭陵蕭琛、北地傅昭、汝南周捨咸稱重之。
units.en: Xiao Chen of Lanling, Fu Zhao of Beidi, and Zhou She of Runan all spoke highly of it.
units.literal: Xiao Chen of Lanling, Fu Zhao of Beidi, and Zhou She of Runan all praised and valued it highly.

units.zh: 至是，吏部尚書徐勉言之於高祖，以爲著作郎，掌國史及起居注。
units.en: At this time Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Mian spoke of him to Emperor Wu, who appointed him Lang of Composition, in charge of the national history and the records of the ruler's movements.
units.literal: At this time Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Mian spoke of him to Gaozu, and he was made Lang of Composition, in charge of the national history and the records of the ruler's movements.

units.zh: 頃之，兼中書通事舍人，尋除通直正員郎，著作、舍人如故。
units.en: Before long he was made concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat; soon afterward he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded, while retaining his posts as Lang of Composition and Attendant.
units.literal: Before long he was made concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat; soon afterward he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded, while his posts as Lang of Composition and Attendant remained as before.

units.zh: 又敕掌中書詔誥。
units.en: He was also ordered to take charge of edicts and proclamations in the Secretariat.
units.literal: He was also ordered to take charge of edicts and proclamations in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 是時西北徼外有白題及滑國，遣使由岷山道入貢。
units.en: At that time beyond the northwestern frontier were the states of Baiti and Hua, which sent envoys along the Minshan route to offer tribute.
units.literal: At that time beyond the northwestern frontier were the states of Baiti and Hua; they sent envoys by the Minshan route to offer tribute.

units.zh: 此二國歷代弗賓，莫知所出。
units.en: These two states had never submitted in any dynasty, and no one knew where they came from.
units.literal: These two states had never submitted in any dynasty, and no one knew whence they came.

units.zh: 子野曰：「漢潁陰侯斬胡白題將一人。
units.en: Ziye said, "In Han, the Marquis of Yingyin beheaded a Baiti general of the Hu.
units.literal: Ziye said, "In Han, Marquis of Yingyin beheaded one Baiti general of the Hu.

units.zh: 服虔《注》云：『白題，胡名也。』
units.en: Fu Qian's commentary says, 'Baiti is a Hu name.'
units.literal: Fu Qian's commentary says: 'Baiti is a Hu name.'

units.zh: 又漢定遠侯擊虜，八滑從之，此其後乎。」
units.en: Moreover, in Han the Marquis of Dingyuan attacked the barbarians, and the Eight Hua followed him — are these their descendants?"
units.literal: Moreover, in Han the Marquis of Dingyuan attacked the barbarians, and the Eight Hua followed him — are these their descendants?"

units.zh: 時人服其博識。
units.en: Men of the time admired his erudition.
units.literal: Men of the time admired his broad learning.

units.zh: 敕仍使撰《方國使圖》，廣述懷來之盛，自要服至于海表，凡二十國。
units.en: He was further ordered to compose the Atlas of Envoys from the Border States, broadly describing the splendor of those who came in allegiance, from the inner domains to beyond the seas — twenty states in all.
units.literal: He was further ordered to compose the Atlas of Envoys from the Border States, broadly setting forth the splendor of those who came in allegiance, from the inner domains to beyond the seas — twenty states in all.

units.zh: 子野與沛國劉顯、南陽劉之遴、陳郡殷芸、陳留阮孝緒、吳郡顧協、京兆韋棱，皆博極羣書，深相賞好，顯尤推重之。
units.en: Ziye, together with Liu Xian of Peiguo, Liu Zhilin of Nanyang, Yin Yun of Chen commandery, Ruan Xiaoxu of Chenliu, Gu Xie of Wu commandery, and Wei Leng of Jingzhao, had all read exhaustively and were close friends; Xian especially esteemed him.
units.literal: Ziye, together with Liu Xian of Peiguo, Liu Zhilin of Nanyang, Yin Yun of Chen commandery, Ruan Xiaoxu of Chenliu, Gu Xie of Wu commandery, and Wei Leng of Jingzhao, all ranged to the utmost through the books and deeply admired and befriended one another; Xian especially valued him.

units.zh: 時吳平侯蕭勱、范陽張纘，每討論墳籍，咸折中於子野焉。
units.en: At that time Marquis of Wuping Xiao Mai and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, whenever they discussed the classics and histories, would all defer to Ziye's judgment.
units.literal: At that time Marquis of Ping of Wu Xiao Mai and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, whenever they discussed the classics and histories, would all defer to Ziye's judgment.

units.zh: 普通七年，王師北伐，敕子野爲喻魏文，受詔立成，高祖以其事體大，召尚書僕射徐勉、太子詹事周捨、鴻臚卿劉之遴、中書侍郎朱异，集壽光殿以觀之，時並嘆服。
units.en: In the seventh year of Putong, the imperial army marched north, and Ziye was ordered to compose a letter admonishing Wei. He received the edict and finished it at once. Because the matter was weighty, Emperor Wu summoned Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Mian, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent Zhou She, Minister of Ceremonies Liu Zhilin, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhu Yi to gather in the Shouguang Hall to read it; all marveled at it.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, the imperial army marched north; Ziye was ordered to compose a letter admonishing Wei. Having received the edict he finished it at once. Gaozu, because the matter was weighty, summoned Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Mian, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent Zhou She, Minister of Ceremonies Liu Zhilin, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhu Yi to gather in the Shouguang Hall to view it; all at once sighed in admiration.

units.zh: 高祖目子野而言曰：「其形雖弱，其文甚壯。」
units.en: Emperor Wu looked at Ziye and said, "His body may be slight, but his writing is very strong."
units.literal: Gaozu looked at Ziye and said, "His form may be frail, but his writing is very strong."

units.zh: 俄又敕爲書喻魏相元乂，其夜受旨，子野謂可待旦方奏，未之爲也。
units.en: Soon afterward he was again ordered to compose a letter admonishing Yuan Yi, chief minister of Wei. That night he received the command; Ziye thought he could wait until dawn before presenting it and did not yet write it.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was again ordered to compose a letter admonishing Yuan Yi, chief minister of Wei. That night he received the command; Ziye thought he could wait until dawn before presenting it and did not yet compose it.

units.zh: 及五鼓，敕催令開齋速上，子野徐起操筆，昧爽便就。
units.en: By the fifth watch an edict urged him to break his fast and submit it quickly. Ziye rose slowly, took up his brush, and by first light it was finished.
units.literal: By the fifth watch an edict urged him to open the fast and submit it quickly. Ziye rose slowly, took up his brush, and by first light it was done.

units.zh: 旣奏，高祖深嘉焉。
units.en: Once it was presented, Emperor Wu praised it highly.
units.literal: Once it was presented, Gaozu deeply praised it.

units.zh: 自是凡諸符檄，皆令草創。
units.en: From then on, all proclamations and dispatches were entrusted to him for drafting.
units.literal: From then on, for all proclamations and dispatches, he was ordered to draft them.

units.zh: 子野爲文典而速，不尚麗靡之詞。
units.en: Ziye wrote in a classical style and with great speed; he did not favor ornate and florid language.
units.literal: Ziye's writing was classical and swift; he did not esteem ornate and florid words.

units.zh: 其制作多法古，與今文體異，當時或有詆訶者，及其末皆翕然重之。
units.en: His compositions largely followed ancient models and differed from contemporary style; some criticized them at the time, but by the end of his life all came to value them.
units.literal: His compositions largely followed antiquity and differed from the style of the present day; at the time some criticized them, but by his end all alike came to value them.

units.zh: 或問其爲文速者，子野答云：「人皆成於手，我獨成於心，雖有見否之異，其於刊改一也。」
units.en: When someone asked about his swift writing, Ziye answered, "Others complete their work with the hand; I alone complete mine in the mind. Though there is a difference between seeing and not seeing, revision is the same either way."
units.literal: When someone asked about his swift writing, Ziye answered, "Others complete their work with the hand; I alone complete mine in the mind. Though there is a difference between seeing and not seeing, in revision it is the same."

units.zh: 俄遷中書侍郎，餘如故。
units.en: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat; his other posts remained unchanged.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat; his other posts remained as before.

units.zh: 大通元年，轉鴻臚卿，尋領步兵校尉。
units.en: In the first year of Datong he was made Minister of Ceremonies, and soon afterward was placed in command as Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong he was made Minister of Ceremonies, and soon afterward was placed in command as Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

units.zh: 子野在禁省十餘年，靜默自守，未嘗有所請謁，外家及中表貧乏，所得俸悉分給之。
units.en: Ziye served in the inner offices for more than ten years, quiet and self-restrained, never making requests or visits. His maternal kin and cousins on his mother's side were poor, and he gave all his salary to them.
units.literal: Ziye was in the inner offices for more than ten years, silent and self-restrained, never making requests or visits. His maternal kin and cousins on his mother's side were poor; all his salary he divided and gave to them.

units.zh: 無宅，借官地二畝，起茅屋數間。
units.en: He had no house of his own and borrowed two mu of government land on which to build a few thatched huts.
units.literal: He had no house and borrowed two mu of government land on which to raise a few thatched huts.

units.zh: 妻子恒苦饑寒，唯以教誨爲本，子侄祗畏，若奉嚴君。
units.en: His wife and children constantly suffered hunger and cold; he took teaching and admonition as his foundation, and his sons and nephews revered him as if he were a stern father.
units.literal: His wife and children constantly suffered hunger and cold; he took instruction and admonition as his foundation, and his sons and nephews revered him as if serving a stern father.

units.zh: 末年深信釋氏，持其教戒，終身飯麥食蔬。
units.en: In his later years he became a devout Buddhist, kept its precepts, and for the rest of his life ate only barley and vegetables.
units.literal: In his later years he deeply believed in the Buddhist teaching, kept its precepts, and for life ate only barley and vegetables.

units.zh: 中大通二年，卒官，年六十二。
units.en: In the second year of Zhongdatong he died in office at the age of sixty-two.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he died in office, age sixty-two.

units.zh: 先是子野自剋死期，不過庚戌歲。
units.en: Earlier Ziye had fixed his own term of death, saying he would not live past the gengxu year.
units.literal: Earlier Ziye had fixed his own term of death, saying it would not pass the gengxu year.

units.zh: 是年自省移病，謂同官劉之亨曰：「吾其逝矣。」
units.en: That year he reported himself ill and withdrew, telling his colleague Liu Zhiheng, "I am about to die."
units.literal: That year he reported himself ill and withdrew, saying to his colleague Liu Zhiheng, "I am about to depart."

units.zh: 遺命儉約，務在節制。
units.en: His final instructions were frugal, with restraint in all things.
units.literal: His final instructions were frugal, striving for restraint.

units.zh: 高祖悼惜，爲之流涕。
units.en: Emperor Wu mourned him deeply and wept for him.
units.literal: Gaozu mourned and cherished his memory, shedding tears for him.

units.zh: 詔曰：「鴻臚卿、領步兵校尉、知著作郎、兼中書通事舍人裴子野，文史足用，廉白自居，劬勞通事，多歷年所。
units.en: An edict said: "Minister of Ceremonies Pei Ziye, who also commanded the Footsoldiers, served as Lang of Composition, and was concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat — his letters and histories were fully adequate, he lived in integrity and purity, and labored diligently in general affairs for many years.
units.literal: An edict said: "Minister of Ceremonies, Colonel of the Footsoldiers in command, Lang of Composition in charge, and concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat Pei Ziye — his letters and histories were fully adequate, he dwelt in integrity and purity, and labored diligently in general affairs for many years.

units.zh: 奄致喪逝，惻愴空懷。
units.en: Suddenly he has died, and our hearts are filled with sorrow and grief.
units.literal: Suddenly he met with death and departure; sorrow and grief fill an empty breast.

units.zh: 可贈散騎常侍，賻錢五萬，布五十匹，卽日舉哀。
units.en: Let him be posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, with funeral gifts of fifty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth; mourning is to begin this very day.
units.literal: He may be posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, with funeral gifts of fifty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth; mourning is to begin this very day.

units.zh: 諡曰貞子。」
units.en: His posthumous title is Zhenzi (Upright)."
units.literal: His posthumous title is Zhenzi (Upright)."

units.zh: 子野少時，《集注喪服》、《續裴氏家傳》各二卷，抄合後漢事四十餘卷，又敕撰《衆僧傳》二十卷，《百官九品》二卷，《附益諡法》一卷，《方國使圖》一卷，文集二十卷，並行於世。
units.en: In his youth Ziye wrote the Collected Commentary on Mourning Garments and the Continuation of the Pei Family Genealogy, each in two juan, and copied and compiled more than forty juan of Later Han affairs. By edict he also composed the Biographies of the Many Monks in twenty juan, the Nine Ranks of the Hundred Officials in two juan, Supplementary Methods of Posthumous Titles in one juan, the Atlas of Envoys from the Border States in one juan, and a collection of writings in twenty juan — all of which circulated in his day.
units.literal: In his youth Ziye wrote the Collected Commentary on Mourning Garments and the Continuation of the Pei Family Genealogy, each in two juan, and copied and compiled more than forty juan of Later Han affairs. By edict he also composed the Biographies of the Many Monks in twenty juan, the Nine Ranks of the Hundred Officials in two juan, Supplementary Methods of Posthumous Titles in one juan, the Atlas of Envoys from the Border States in one juan, and a collection of writings in twenty juan — all circulated in the world.

units.zh: 又欲撰《齊梁春秋》，始草創，未就而卒。
units.en: He also wished to compose the Spring and Autumn of Qi and Liang, but had only begun the draft when he died without finishing it.
units.literal: He also wished to compose the Spring and Autumn of Qi and Liang, but had only begun the draft when he died before completing it.

units.zh: 子謇，官至通直郎。
units.en: His son Pei Jian rose to the office of Attendant of the Unimpeded.
units.literal: His son Jian reached the office of Attendant of the Unimpeded.

units.zh: 顧協字正禮，吳郡吳人也。
units.en: Gu Xie, styled Zhengli, came from Wu in Wu commandery.
units.literal: Gu Xie, styled Zhengli, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.

units.zh: 晉司空和七世孫。
units.en: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Gu He, who had served Jin as Minister of Works.
units.literal: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Gu He, Minister of Works of Jin.

units.zh: 協幼孤，隨母養於外氏。
units.en: Xie lost his father early and was raised with his mother in his maternal family's household.
units.literal: Xie was orphaned young and was raised with his mother in his maternal family's household.

units.zh: 外從祖宋右光祿張永嘗攜內外孫侄游虎丘山，協年數歲，永撫之曰：「兒欲何戲？」
units.en: His maternal great-uncle Zhang Yong, who had served Song as Right Director of the Imperial Secretariat, once took the inner and outer grandsons and nephews to tour Tiger Hill. Xie was only a few years old; Yong stroked him and said, "Child, what would you like to play?"
units.literal: His maternal great-uncle Zhang Yong, Right Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Song, once took the inner and outer grandsons and nephews to tour Tiger Hill. Xie was only a few years old; Yong stroked him and said, "Child, what game do you wish to play?"

units.zh: 協對曰：「兒正欲枕石漱流。」
units.en: Xie replied, "This child wishes only to pillow himself on stone and rinse his mouth in the stream."
units.literal: Xie replied, "This child wishes only to pillow himself on stone and rinse his mouth in the stream."

units.zh: 永歎息曰：「顧氏興於此子。」
units.en: Yong sighed and said, "The Gu clan will rise through this child."
units.literal: Yong sighed and said, "The Gu clan will rise through this child."

units.zh: 旣長，好學，以精力稱。
units.en: When he grew up he loved study and was known for his vigor and energy.
units.literal: When he grew up he loved learning and was known for his vigor and energy.

units.zh: 外氏諸張多賢達有識鑒，從內弟率尤推重焉。
units.en: The Zhangs of his maternal family were mostly worthy and discerning; his cousin on his mother's side, Zhang Shuai, especially esteemed him.
units.literal: The Zhangs of his maternal family were mostly worthy and discerning; his cousin on his mother's side, Zhang Shuai, especially valued and esteemed him.

units.zh: 起家揚州議曹從事史，兼太學博士。
units.en: He entered service as a clerk in the deliberation office of Yangzhou and as concurrent Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
units.literal: He began his career as a clerk in the deliberation office of Yangzhou and as concurrent Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 舉秀才，尚書令沈約覽其策而歎曰：「江左以來，未有此作。」
units.en: He was recommended as a cultivated talent. When Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue read his examination essay, he sighed and said, "Since the south of the Yangtze, there has been nothing like this."
units.literal: He was recommended as a cultivated talent. Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue read his examination essay and sighed, "Since the south of the Yangtze, there has been nothing like this composition."

units.zh: 遷安成王國左常侍，兼廷尉正。
units.en: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of the Prince of Ancheng and made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.
units.literal: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of the Prince of Ancheng and made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.

units.zh: 太尉臨川王聞其名，召掌書記，仍侍西豊侯正德讀。
units.en: The Defender-in-Chief, Prince of Linchuan, heard his name and summoned him to take charge of records, and he also attended upon Marquis of Feng of the West, Xiao Zhengde, in his studies.
units.literal: The Defender-in-Chief, Prince of Linchuan, heard his name and summoned him to take charge of records, and he also attended upon Marquis of Feng of the West, Xiao Zhengde, in his studies.

units.zh: 正德爲巴西、梓潼郡，協除所部安都令。
units.en: Zhengde held the commanderies of Baxi and Zitong; Xie was appointed magistrate of Andu within his jurisdiction.
units.literal: Zhengde held the commanderies of Baxi and Zitong; Xie was appointed magistrate of Andu within his jurisdiction.

units.zh: 未至縣，遭母憂。
units.en: Before he reached the county, his mother died.
units.literal: Before he reached the county he met with his mother's death.

units.zh: 服闋，出補西陽郡丞。
units.en: When mourning ended, he was sent out as assistant administrator of Xiyang commandery.
units.literal: When mourning ended he went out to fill the post of assistant administrator of Xiyang commandery.

units.zh: 還除北中郎行參軍，復兼廷尉正。
units.en: On his return he was appointed acting aide to the Northern Central Commandant and again made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.
units.literal: On his return he was appointed acting aide to the Northern Central Commandant and again made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.

units.zh: 久之，出爲廬陵郡丞，未拜。
units.en: After some time he was appointed assistant administrator of Luling commandery but did not assume the post.
units.literal: After some time he was sent out as assistant administrator of Luling commandery but did not assume the post.

units.zh: 會西豊侯正德爲吳郡，除中軍參軍，領郡五官，遷輕車湘東王參軍事，兼記室。
units.en: When Marquis of Feng of the West Zhengde became governor of Wu commandery, Xie was appointed aide in the Central Army and placed in charge of the five officials of the commandery; he was then transferred as aide to the Prince of Xiangdong in the Light Chariots and made concurrent recorder.
units.literal: When Marquis of Feng of the West Zhengde became governor of Wu commandery, Xie was appointed aide in the Central Army and placed in charge of the five officials of the commandery; he was then transferred as aide to the Prince of Xiangdong in the Light Chariots and made concurrent recorder.

units.zh: 普通六年，正德受詔北討，引爲府錄事參軍，掌書記。
units.en: In the sixth year of Putong, Zhengde received an edict for the northern campaign and took Xie on as recorder of the headquarters, in charge of records.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Putong, Zhengde received an edict for the northern campaign and took him on as recorder of the headquarters, in charge of records.

units.zh: 軍還，會有詔舉士，湘東王表薦協曰：「臣聞貢玉之士，歸之潤山；
units.en: When the army returned, an edict called for the recommendation of scholars. The Prince of Xiangdong memorialized recommending Xie, saying, "Your servant has heard that one who offers jade returns to Mount Run;
units.literal: When the army returned, there happened to be an edict calling for the recommendation of scholars. The Prince of Xiangdong memorialized recommending Xie, saying: "Your servant has heard that one who offers jade returns to Mount Run;

units.zh: 論珠之人，出於枯岸。
units.en: and one who assesses pearls comes forth from a barren shore.
units.literal: and one who discusses pearls comes forth from a withered bank.

units.zh: 是以芻蕘之言，擇於廊廟者也。
units.en: That is why the humble words of common folk may be chosen in the halls of state.
units.literal: Therefore the words of hay-cutters and firewood-gatherers are chosen in the court and temple.

units.zh: 臣府兼記室參軍吳郡顧協，行稱鄉閭，學兼文武，服膺道素，雅量邃遠，安貧守靜，奉公抗直，傍闕知己，志不自營，年方六十，室無妻子。
units.en: Your servant's headquarters concurrent recorder Gu Xie of Wu commandery — his conduct is praised throughout his district, his learning embraces both civil and military affairs, he embraces the Way in plain simplicity, his generous spirit runs deep, he is content in poverty and keeps to quiet, serves the public with upright integrity, has no patron at his side, and never seeks his own advantage. He is just sixty, and his household has neither wife nor children.
units.literal: Your servant's headquarters concurrent recorder Gu Xie of Wu commandery — his conduct is praised in village and district, his learning embraces both civil and military affairs, he embraces the Way in plain simplicity, his generous measure is deep and far-reaching, he is content in poverty and keeps to quiet, serves the public with upright integrity, lacks a patron at his side, and his will does not seek its own ends. He is just sixty, and his household has neither wife nor children.

units.zh: 臣欲言于官人，申其屈滯，協必苦執貞退，立志難奪，可謂東南之遺寶矣。
units.en: Your servant wished to speak to the officials on his behalf, but Xie would surely cling stubbornly to integrity and withdrawal; his resolve cannot be swayed. He may truly be called a treasure left behind in the southeast.
units.literal: Your servant wished to speak to the officials and set forth how he has been held back and neglected, but Xie would surely cling bitterly to integrity and withdrawal; his resolve is hard to sway. He may be called a treasure left behind in the southeast.

units.zh: 伏惟陛下未明求衣，思賢如渴，爰發明詔，各舉所知。
units.en: I bow my head and consider that Your Majesty, rising before dawn to seek your robes, thirsts for the worthy as for water, and has therefore issued a bright edict that each should recommend those he knows.
units.literal: I bow my head and consider that Your Majesty, before dawn seeks your robes, thirsts for the worthy as for water, and has therefore issued a bright edict that each should recommend those he knows.

units.zh: 臣識非許、郭，雖無知人之鑒，若守固無言，懼貽蔽賢之咎。
units.en: Your servant's discernment does not match that of Xu and Guo; though I lack the eye for knowing men, if I kept stubbornly silent I would fear the fault of concealing the worthy.
units.literal: Your servant's discernment does not match that of Xu and Guo; though I lack the eye for knowing men, if I kept silent out of stubbornness I would fear the fault of concealing the worthy.

units.zh: 昔孔愉表韓績之才，庾亮薦翟湯之德，臣雖未齒二臣，協實無慚兩士。」
units.en: In the past Kong Yu memorialized Han Ji's talent and Yu Liang recommended Zhai Tang's virtue. Your servant, though not equal to those two ministers, finds that Xie would not be shamed before those two gentlemen."
units.literal: In the past Kong Yu memorialized Han Ji's talent and Yu Liang recommended Zhai Tang's virtue. Your servant, though not equal to those two ministers, finds that Xie is truly not shamed before those two gentlemen."

units.zh: 卽召拜通直散騎侍郎，兼中書通事舍人。
units.en: He was at once summoned and appointed Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry and made concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat.
units.literal: He was at once summoned and appointed Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry and made concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 累遷步兵校尉，守鴻臚卿，員外散騎常侍，卿、舍人並如故。
units.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of the Footsoldiers, acting Minister of Ceremonies, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; his posts as minister and attendant remained unchanged.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of the Footsoldiers, acting Minister of Ceremonies, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; his posts as minister and attendant remained as before.

units.zh: 大同八年，卒，時年七十三。
units.en: In the eighth year of Datong he died at the age of seventy-three.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Datong he died, age seventy-three.

units.zh: 高祖悼惜之，手詔曰：「員外散騎常侍、鴻臚卿、兼中書通事舍人顧協，廉潔自居，白首不衰，久在省闥，內外稱善。
units.en: Emperor Wu mourned him deeply and wrote in his own hand: "Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Gu Xie, who also served as Minister of Ceremonies and concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat — he lived in integrity and purity, which did not fade even in old age. Long in the inner offices, he was praised within and without.
units.literal: Gaozu mourned and cherished him, writing in his own hand: "Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, Minister of Ceremonies, and concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat Gu Xie — he dwelt in integrity and purity, which did not fade even in white-haired old age. Long in the inner offices, he was praised within and without.

units.zh: 奄然殞喪，惻怛之懷，不能已已。
units.en: Suddenly he has died, and sorrow in my breast cannot cease.
units.literal: Suddenly he has met with death and departure; sorrow and grief in the breast cannot cease.

units.zh: 傍無近親，彌足哀者。
units.en: He has no close kin at his side — this makes the grief all the greater.
units.literal: He has no close kin at his side — this makes the grief all the greater.

units.zh: 大殮旣畢，卽送其喪柩還鄉，並營冢槨，並皆資給，悉使周辦。
units.en: Once the encoffinment is complete, send his bier back to his native place at once, provide for his tomb and coffin, supply everything needed, and have it all fully arranged.
units.literal: Once the great encoffinment is complete, send his bier back to his native place at once, and also provide for his tomb and coffin — supply everything and have it all fully arranged.

units.zh: 可贈散騎常侍，令便舉哀。
units.en: Let him be posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and let mourning begin at once.
units.literal: He may be posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and mourning is to begin at once.

units.zh: 諡曰溫子。」
units.en: His posthumous title is Wenzi (Gentle)."
units.literal: His posthumous title is Wenzi (Gentle)."

units.zh: 協少清介有志操。
units.en: From youth Xie was pure, upright, and possessed of moral resolve.
units.literal: Xie from youth was pure, upright, and possessed of moral resolve.

units.zh: 初爲廷尉正，冬服單薄，寺卿蔡法度謂人曰：「我願解身上襦與顧郎，恐顧郎難衣食者。」
units.en: When he first served as Director of the Court of Justice, his winter clothing was thin. Director Cai Fadu of the bureau said to others, "I would gladly take off my own jacket and give it to Master Gu, but I fear he would find it hard to accept clothing and food."
units.literal: When he first served as Director of the Court of Justice, his winter clothing was thin. Director Cai Fadu of the bureau said to others, "I would gladly take off my own jacket and give it to Master Gu, but I fear Master Gu would find it hard to accept clothing and food."

units.zh: 竟不敢以遺之。
units.en: In the end he did not dare give it to him.
units.literal: In the end he did not dare give it to him.

units.zh: 及爲舍人，同官者皆潤屋，協在省十六載，器服飲食，不改於常。
units.en: When he became an attendant, his colleagues all enriched their households, but Xie served in the inner offices for sixteen years and his utensils, clothing, food, and drink never changed from the usual.
units.literal: When he became an attendant, his colleagues all enriched their houses, but Xie was in the inner offices for sixteen years and his utensils, clothing, food, and drink never changed from the usual.

units.zh: 有門生始來事協，知其廉潔，不敢厚餉，止送錢二千，協發怒，杖二十，因此事者絕於饋遺。
units.en: A student who had just come to serve Xie, knowing his integrity, did not dare make a lavish gift and sent only two thousand cash. Xie grew angry and had him beaten twenty strokes; from then on those who served him ceased all gifts.
units.literal: A student who had just come to serve Xie, knowing his integrity and purity, did not dare make a lavish gift and sent only two thousand cash. Xie grew angry and had him beaten twenty strokes; from then on those who served him ceased all gifts.

units.zh: 自丁艱憂，遂終身布衣蔬食。
units.en: From the time he mourned his mother, for the rest of his life he wore plain cloth and ate only vegetables.
units.literal: From the time he entered mourning for his mother, for the rest of his life he wore plain cloth and ate vegetables.

units.zh: 少時將娉舅息女，未成婚而協母亡，免喪後不復娶。
units.en: In youth he was betrothed to his uncle's son's daughter, but before the marriage was completed his mother died; after mourning ended he did not marry again.
units.literal: In youth he was betrothed to his uncle's son's daughter, but before the marriage was completed Xie's mother died; after mourning ended he did not marry again.

units.zh: 至六十餘，此女猶未他適，協義而迎之。
units.en: By his sixties this woman had still not married another; out of righteousness Xie went to receive her as his wife.
units.literal: By his sixties this woman had still not married another; out of righteousness Xie went to receive her.

units.zh: 晚雖判合，卒無胤嗣。
units.en: Though late in life they were joined, in the end he had no heirs.
units.literal: Though late in life they were joined, in the end he had no heirs.

units.zh: 協博極羣書，於文字及禽獸草木尤稱精詳。
units.en: Xie had read exhaustively and was especially renowned for his precision in writing and in birds, beasts, plants, and trees.
units.literal: Xie ranged to the utmost through all books and was especially praised as precise and thorough in writing and in birds, beasts, plants, and trees.

units.zh: 撰《異姓苑》五卷，《瑣語》十卷，並行於世。
units.en: He composed the Garden of Variant Surnames in five juan and Trivial Sayings in ten juan, both of which circulated in his day.
units.literal: He composed the Garden of Variant Surnames in five juan and Trivial Sayings in ten juan, both circulating in the world.

units.zh: 徐摛字士秀，東海郯人也。
units.en: Xu Chi, styled Shixiu, came from Tan in Donghai.
units.literal: Xu Chi, styled Shixiu, was a native of Tan in Donghai.

units.zh: 祖憑道，宋海陵太守。
units.en: His grandfather Xu Pingdao had been governor of Hailing under the Song.
units.literal: His grandfather Pingdao was governor of Hailing under Song.

units.zh: 父超之，天監初仕至員外散騎常侍。
units.en: His father Xu Chaozhi, early in the Tianjian era, rose to Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
units.literal: His father Chaozhi, at the beginning of Tianjian, rose in office to Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

units.zh: 摛幼而好學，及長，遍覽經史。
units.en: From youth Chi loved study; when he grew up he read widely in the classics and histories.
units.literal: Chi from youth loved learning; when he grew up he ranged through the classics and histories.

units.zh: 屬文好爲新變，不拘舊體。
units.en: In writing he loved innovation and was not bound by older forms.
units.literal: In composing texts he loved to make new changes and was not bound by old forms.

units.zh: 起家太學博士，遷左衛司馬。
units.en: He entered service as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Marshal of the Left Guard.
units.literal: He began his career as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Marshal of the Left Guard.

units.zh: 會晉安王綱出戍石頭，高祖謂周捨曰：「爲我求一人，文學俱長兼有行者，欲令與晉安遊處。」
units.en: When Prince Jin'an Xiao Gang went out to garrison Shitou, Emperor Wu said to Zhou She, "Find me a man accomplished in both letters and learning who also has proper conduct, to keep company with Jin'an."
units.literal: When Prince Jin'an Gang went out to garrison Shitou, Gaozu said to Zhou She, "Find me a man accomplished in both letters and learning who also has conduct, whom I wish to have keep company with Jin'an."

units.zh: 捨曰：「臣外弟徐摛，形質陋小，若不勝衣，而堪此選。」
units.en: She said, "Your servant's cousin on his mother's side Xu Chi — his frame is slight and homely, as if he could not fill his clothes, yet he is fit for this selection."
units.literal: She said, "Your servant's cousin on his mother's side Xu Chi — his form and substance are homely and slight, as if he could not fill his clothes, yet he is fit for this selection."

units.zh: 高祖曰：「必有仲宣之才，亦不簡其容貌。」
units.en: Emperor Wu said, "If he has the talent of Wang Can, I will not be choosy about his appearance."
units.literal: Gaozu said, "If he has the talent of Zhongxuan, I will not be choosy about his appearance."

units.zh: 以摛爲侍讀。
units.en: Chi was made study companion to the prince.
units.literal: Chi was made study companion.

units.zh: 後王出鎮江州，仍補雲麾府記室參軍，又轉平西府中記室。
units.en: Later the prince went out to govern Jiangzhou; Chi was appointed recorder for the Cloud Pennant headquarters and then transferred to central recorder for the Pacify-the-West headquarters.
units.literal: Later the prince went out to govern Jiangzhou; Chi was appointed recorder for the Cloud Pennant headquarters and then transferred to central recorder for the Pacify-the-West headquarters.

units.zh: 王移鎮京口，復隨府轉爲安北中錄事參軍，帶郯令，以母憂去職。
units.en: When the prince moved his garrison to Jingkou, Chi followed the headquarters and was made recorder for the Pacify-the-North Central Commandant, with concurrent appointment as magistrate of Tan; he resigned when his mother died.
units.literal: When the prince moved his garrison to Jingkou, Chi again followed the headquarters and was made recorder for the Pacify-the-North Central Commandant, with concurrent appointment as magistrate of Tan; he left office upon his mother's death.

units.zh: 王爲丹陽尹，起摛爲秣陵令。
units.en: When the prince became governor of Danyang, Chi was recalled as magistrate of Moling.
units.literal: When the prince became governor of Danyang, Chi was recalled as magistrate of Moling.

units.zh: 普通四年，王出鎮襄陽，摛固求隨府西上，遷晉安王諮議參軍。
units.en: In the fourth year of Putong the prince went out to govern Xiangyang; Chi firmly requested to follow the headquarters west and was promoted to advisory aide to Prince Jin'an.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Putong the prince went out to govern Xiangyang; Chi firmly requested to follow the headquarters west and was promoted to advisory aide to Prince Jin'an.

units.zh: 大通初，王總戎北伐，以摛兼寧蠻府長史，參贊戎政，教命軍書，多自摛出。
units.en: At the beginning of Datong the prince took overall command of the northern campaign; Chi was made concurrent Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-Barbarians headquarters and assisted in military affairs; instructions and military documents mostly came from Chi.
units.literal: At the beginning of Datong the prince took overall command of the northern campaign; Chi was made concurrent Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-Barbarians headquarters, assisting in military affairs; instructions and military documents mostly came from Chi.

units.zh: 王入爲皇太子，轉家令，兼掌管記，尋帶領直。
units.en: When the prince entered the capital as crown prince, Chi was transferred to Director of the Palace Household, with concurrent charge of records, and soon afterward was placed in command of the direct guard.
units.literal: When the prince entered the capital as crown prince, Chi was transferred to Director of the Palace Household, with concurrent charge of records, and soon afterward was placed in command of the direct guard.

units.zh: 摛文體旣別，春坊盡學之，「宮體」之號，自斯而起。
units.en: Chi's literary style was already distinctive; the crown prince's household all studied it, and the name "Palace Style" arose from this.
units.literal: Chi's literary style was already distinctive; the Eastern Palace all studied it, and the name "Palace Style" arose from this.

units.zh: 高祖聞之怒，召摛加讓，及見，應對明敏，辭義可觀，高祖意釋。
units.en: Emperor Wu heard of it and grew angry; he summoned Chi to reproach him, but when he saw him, Chi's replies were clear and keen and his words were impressive; the emperor's anger lifted.
units.literal: Gaozu heard of it and grew angry; he summoned Chi to reproach him, but when he saw him, Chi's replies were clear and keen and his words and meaning were worth viewing; Gaozu's anger lifted.

units.zh: 因問《五經》大義，次問歷代史及百家雜說，末論釋教。
units.en: He then asked about the great meaning of the Five Classics, next about histories of successive dynasties and miscellaneous writings of the hundred schools, and finally discussed Buddhism.
units.literal: He then asked about the great meaning of the Five Classics, next about histories of successive dynasties and miscellaneous writings of the hundred schools, and finally discussed the Buddhist teaching.

units.zh: 摛商較縱橫，應答如響，高祖甚加歎異，更被親狎，寵遇日隆。
units.en: Chi debated freely and answered like an echo; Emperor Wu marveled at him, drew him closer, and his favor grew daily.
units.literal: Chi weighed and compared freely, answering like an echo; Gaozu greatly sighed in wonder, drew him closer in intimacy, and his favor and treatment grew daily.

units.zh: 領軍朱异不說，謂所親曰：「徐叟出入兩宮，漸來逼我，須早爲之所。」
units.en: Commandant-in-Chief Zhu Yi was displeased and said to those close to him, "Old Xu goes in and out of both palaces and is gradually pressing upon me; I must deal with this early."
units.literal: Commandant-in-Chief Zhu Yi was displeased and said to those close to him, "Old Xu goes in and out of both palaces and is gradually pressing upon me; I must deal with this early."

units.zh: 遂承間白高祖曰：「摛年老，又愛泉石，意在一郡，以自怡養。」
units.en: He then seized an opportunity to inform Emperor Wu, saying, "Chi is old and loves springs and rocks; his wish is for one commandery where he may nourish himself in ease."
units.literal: He then seized an opportunity to inform Gaozu, saying, "Chi is old and also loves springs and rocks; his wish is for one commandery where he may nourish himself in ease."

units.zh: 高祖謂摛欲之，乃召摛曰：「新安大好山水，任昉等並經爲之，卿爲我臥治此郡。」
units.en: Emperor Wu thought Chi wished it and summoned him, saying, "Xin'an has excellent mountains and waters; Ren Fang and others have all governed it. You shall govern this commandery for me from your couch."
units.literal: Gaozu thought Chi wished it and therefore summoned him, saying, "Xin'an has excellent mountains and waters; Ren Fang and others have all governed it. You shall lie abed and govern this commandery for me."

units.zh: 中大通三年，遂出爲新安太守。
units.en: In the third year of Zhongdatong he was sent out as governor of Xin'an.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong he went out as governor of Xin'an.

units.zh: 至郡，爲治清靜，教民禮義，勸課農桑，期月之中，風俗便改。
units.en: On reaching the commandery he governed with purity and quiet, taught the people rites and righteousness, and urged them in agriculture and sericulture; within a month customs were transformed.
units.literal: On reaching the commandery he governed with purity and quiet, taught the people rites and righteousness, and urged them in agriculture and sericulture; within a full month customs were changed.

units.zh: 秩滿，還爲中庶子，加戎昭將軍。
units.en: When his term ended he returned as Central Palace Companion and was given the additional title General Who Displays Martial Resolution.
units.literal: When his term ended he returned as Central Palace Companion and was given the additional title General Who Displays Martial Resolution.

units.zh: 是時臨城公納夫人王氏，卽太宗妃之侄女也。
units.en: At that time Duke of Lincheng took Lady Wang as his consort — she was the niece of Emperor Jianwen's consort.
units.literal: At that time Duke of Lincheng took Lady Wang as his consort — she was the niece of Taizong's consort.

units.zh: 晉宋已來，初婚三日，婦見舅姑，衆賓皆列觀，引《春秋》義云「丁丑，夫人姜氏至。
units.en: Since Jin and Song, on the third day after the first marriage the wife would see her husband's parents, and all the guests would stand in rows to observe, citing the Spring and Autumn Annals: "On dingchou the lady, née Jiang, arrived.
units.literal: Since Jin and Song, on the third day after the first marriage the wife would see her husband's parents, and all the guests would stand in rows to observe, citing the meaning in the Spring and Autumn Annals: "On dingchou the lady, née Jiang, arrived.

units.zh: 戊寅，公使大夫宗婦覿用幣」。
units.en: On wuyin the duke sent a grandee and a clan wife to perform the presentation audience with gifts."
units.literal: On wuyin the duke sent a grandee and a clan wife to perform the presentation audience with gifts."

units.zh: 戊寅，丁丑之明日，故禮官據此，皆云宜依舊貫。
units.en: Wuyin was the day after dingchou; therefore the ritual officers, relying on this, all said the old practice should be followed.
units.literal: Wuyin was the day after dingchou; therefore the ritual officers, relying on this, all said the old practice should be followed.

units.zh: 太宗以問摛，摛曰：「《儀禮》云『質明贊見婦于舅姑』。
units.en: Emperor Jianwen asked Chi about it. Chi said, "The Ceremonies say, 'At first light the sponsor presents the wife to the husband's parents.'
units.literal: Taizong asked Chi about it. Chi said, "The Ceremonies say, 'At first light the sponsor presents the wife to the husband's parents.'

units.zh: 《雜記》又云『婦見舅姑，兄弟姊妹皆立于堂下』。
units.en: The Miscellaneous Records also say, 'When the wife sees her husband's parents, brothers and sisters all stand below the hall.'
units.literal: The Miscellaneous Records also say, 'When the wife sees her husband's parents, brothers and sisters all stand below the hall.'

units.zh: 政言婦是外宗，未審嫻令，所以停坐三朝，觀其七德。
units.en: This means the wife is of an outside clan and her skill and obedience are not yet known; therefore she is made to remain seated through three mornings while her seven virtues are observed.
units.literal: This means the wife is of an outside clan and her skill and obedience are not yet known; therefore she is made to remain seated through three mornings while her seven virtues are observed.

units.zh: 舅延外客，姑率內賓，堂下之儀，以備盛禮。
units.en: The father-in-law receives outside guests, the mother-in-law leads inside guests — the ceremony below the hall completes the full rite.
units.literal: The father-in-law receives outside guests, the mother-in-law leads inside guests — the ceremony below the hall is to complete the full rite.

units.zh: 近代婦於舅姑，本有戚屬，不相瞻看。
units.en: In recent times wives and their husbands' parents already had kin ties and did not face one another in audience.
units.literal: In recent times wives and their husbands' parents already had kin ties and did not face one another in audience.

units.zh: 夫人乃妃侄女，有異他姻，覿見之儀，謂應可略。」
units.en: This lady is the niece of the consort and differs from other marriages; the presentation audience, I hold, may be abbreviated."
units.literal: This lady is the niece of the consort and differs from other marriages; the presentation audience, I hold, may be abbreviated."

units.zh: 太宗從其議。
units.en: Emperor Jianwen followed his opinion.
units.literal: Taizong followed his opinion.

units.zh: 除太子左衛率。
units.en: He was appointed Left Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard.
units.literal: He was appointed Left Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard.

units.zh: 太清三年，侯景攻陷臺城，時太宗居永福省，賊衆奔入，舉兵上殿，侍衛奔散，莫有存者。
units.en: In the third year of Taiqing, Hou Jing captured Terrace City. At that time Emperor Jianwen resided in the Yongfu quarter; the rebel host rushed in, raised arms, and ascended the hall. The guards fled and scattered; none remained.
units.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, Hou Jing captured and overran Terrace City. At that time Taizong resided in the Yongfu quarter; the rebel host rushed in, raised arms, and ascended the hall. The guards fled and scattered; none remained.

units.zh: 摛獨嶷然侍立不動，徐謂景曰：「侯公當以禮見，何得如此。」
units.en: Chi alone stood attendant, lofty and unmoving, and slowly said to Jing, "Lord Hou ought to be received with proper ceremony — how can you act like this?"
units.literal: Chi alone stood attendant, lofty and unmoving, and slowly said to Jing, "Lord Hou ought to be received with rites — how can you act like this?"

units.zh: 凶威遂折。
units.en: His fierce authority was thereby broken.
units.literal: His fierce authority was thereby broken.

units.zh: 侯景乃拜，由是常憚摛。
units.en: Hou Jing then bowed; from this he always feared Chi.
units.literal: Hou Jing then bowed; from this he always feared Chi.

units.zh: 太宗嗣位，進授左衛將軍，固辭不拜。
units.en: When Emperor Jianwen succeeded to the throne, Chi was advanced to General of the Left Guard, but he firmly declined and did not accept.
units.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Chi was advanced and given the post of General of the Left Guard, but he firmly declined and did not accept.

units.zh: 太宗後被幽閉，摛不獲朝謁，因感氣疾而卒，年七十八。
units.en: Later Emperor Jianwen was confined in seclusion; Chi could not attend court and, afflicted by illness, died at the age of seventy-eight.
units.literal: Later Taizong was confined in seclusion; Chi could not attend court audience and, afflicted by a disorder of the vital breath, died, age seventy-eight.

units.zh: 長子陵，最知名。
units.en: His eldest son Xu Ling was the most famous.
units.literal: His eldest son Ling was the most famous.

units.zh: 鮑泉字潤岳，東海人也。
units.en: Bao Quan, styled Runyue, came from Donghai.
units.literal: Bao Quan, styled Runyue, was a native of Donghai.

units.zh: 父機，湘東王諮議參軍。
units.en: His father Bao Ji was advisory aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.
units.literal: His father Ji was advisory aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.

units.zh: 泉博涉史傳，兼有文筆。
units.en: Quan ranged broadly through histories and biographies and was also accomplished as a writer.
units.literal: Quan ranged broadly through histories and biographies and was also accomplished with the brush.

units.zh: 少事元帝，早見擢任。
units.en: In youth he served Emperor Yuan and was early selected for appointment.
units.literal: In youth he served Emperor Yuan and was early selected and appointed.

units.zh: 及元帝承制，累遷至信州刺史。
units.en: When Emperor Yuan assumed the regency he was repeatedly promoted to regional inspector of Xinzhou.
units.literal: When Emperor Yuan assumed the regency he was repeatedly promoted to regional inspector of Xinzhou.

units.zh: 太清三年，元帝命泉征河東王譽於湘州，泉至長沙，作連城以逼之，譽率衆攻泉，泉據柵堅守，譽不能克。
units.en: In the third year of Taiqing, Emperor Yuan ordered Quan to campaign against Prince Hedong Xiao Yu in Xiangzhou. Quan reached Changsha and built linked ramparts to press him; Yu led his forces to attack Quan, but Quan held the palisade and defended firmly, and Yu could not overcome him.
units.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, Emperor Yuan ordered Quan to campaign against Prince Hedong Yu in Xiangzhou. Quan reached Changsha and built linked ramparts to press him; Yu led his host to attack Quan, but Quan held the palisade and defended firmly, and Yu could not overcome him.

units.zh: 泉因其弊出擊之，譽大敗，盡俘其衆，遂圍其城，久未能拔。
units.en: Quan, taking advantage of his weakness, sallied forth and struck him; Yu was greatly defeated and his entire force was captured. Quan then besieged his city but for a long time could not take it.
units.literal: Quan, taking advantage of his weakness, sallied forth and struck him; Yu was greatly defeated and his entire host was captured. Quan then besieged his city but for a long time could not take it.

units.zh: 世祖乃數泉罪，遣平南將軍王僧辯代泉爲都督。
units.en: Emperor Yuan then enumerated Quan's crimes and sent General Who Pacifies the South Wang Sengbian to replace Quan as commander-in-chief.
units.literal: Shizu then enumerated Quan's crimes and sent General Who Pacifies the South Wang Sengbian to replace Quan as commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 僧辯至，泉愕然，顧左右曰：「得王竟陵助我經略，賊不足平矣。」
units.en: When Sengbian arrived, Quan was startled and, turning to those at his side, said, "With Wang of Jingling to assist me in strategy, the rebels are not worth pacifying."
units.literal: When Sengbian arrived, Quan was startled and, turning to those at his side, said, "With Wang of Jingling to assist me in strategy, the rebels are not worth pacifying."

units.zh: 僧辯旣入，乃背泉而坐，曰：「鮑郎有罪，令旨使我鎖卿，卿勿以故意見期。」
units.en: Once Sengbian had entered, he sat with his back to Quan and said, "Master Bao is guilty; by command I am to lock you up — do not expect old friendship."
units.literal: Once Sengbian had entered, he sat with his back to Quan and said, "Master Bao is guilty; by command I am to lock you up — do not expect old friendship."

units.zh: 因出令示泉，鎖之床下。
units.en: He then produced the order and showed it to Quan, and locked him beneath the bed.
units.literal: He then produced the order and showed it to Quan, and locked him beneath the bed.

units.zh: 泉曰：「稽緩王師，甘罪是分，但恐後人更思鮑泉之憒憒耳。」
units.en: Quan said, "In delaying the imperial army I accept my share of guilt, but I fear later men will again think of Bao Quan's muddle-headedness."
units.literal: Quan said, "In delaying the imperial army I accept my share of guilt, but I fear later men will again think of Bao Quan's muddle-headedness."

units.zh: 乃爲啓謝淹遲之罪。
units.en: He then composed a memorial apologizing for the offense of delay.
units.literal: He then composed a memorial apologizing for the offense of delay.

units.zh: 世祖尋復其任，令與僧辯等率舟師東逼邵陵王於郢州。
units.en: Emperor Yuan soon restored him to his post and ordered him, together with Sengbian and others, to lead the fleet east and press Prince Shaoling at Yingzhou.
units.literal: Shizu soon restored him to his post and ordered him, together with Sengbian and others, to lead the fleet east and press Prince Shaoling at Yingzhou.

units.zh: 郢州平，元帝以長子方諸爲刺史，泉爲長史，行府州事。
units.en: When Yingzhou was pacified, Emperor Yuan appointed his eldest son Fangzhu regional inspector; Quan was made Chief Clerk and administered the headquarters and province.
units.literal: When Yingzhou was pacified, Emperor Yuan appointed his eldest son Fangzhu regional inspector; Quan was made Chief Clerk and acted in the affairs of the headquarters and province.

units.zh: 侯景密遣將宋子仙、任約率精騎襲之。
units.en: Hou Jing secretly sent his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to lead picked cavalry in a surprise attack.
units.literal: Hou Jing secretly sent his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to lead picked cavalry in a surprise attack.

units.zh: 方諸與泉不恤軍政，唯蒲酒自樂，賊騎至，百姓奔告，方諸與泉方雙陸，不信，曰：「徐文盛大軍在東，賊何由得至？」
units.en: Fangzhu and Quan paid no attention to military affairs and took their pleasure only in gambling and wine. When the rebel cavalry arrived, the common folk ran to report it; Fangzhu and Quan were just playing backgammon and did not believe it, saying, "Xu Wensheng's great army is in the east — how could the rebels get here?"
units.literal: Fangzhu and Quan did not attend to military affairs and took their pleasure only in gambling and wine. When the rebel cavalry arrived, the common folk ran to report it; Fangzhu and Quan were just playing backgammon and did not believe it, saying, "Xu Wensheng's great army is in the east — how could the rebels get here?"

units.zh: 旣而傳告者衆，始令闔門。
units.en: Before long those who came to report were many, and only then did they order the gates closed.
units.literal: Before long those who came to report were many, and only then did they order the gates closed.

units.zh: 賊縱火焚之，莫有抗者，賊騎遂入，城乃陷。
units.en: The rebels set fires to burn the gates; none resisted, the rebel cavalry then entered, and the city fell.
units.literal: The rebels set fires to burn them; none resisted, the rebel cavalry then entered, and the city fell.

units.zh: 執方諸及泉送之景所。
units.en: They seized Fangzhu and Quan and sent them to Hou Jing's headquarters.
units.literal: They seized Fangzhu and Quan and sent them to Jing's headquarters.

units.zh: 後景攻王僧辯於巴陵，不克，敗還，乃殺泉於江夏，沉其屍于黃鵠磯。
units.en: Later Hou Jing attacked Wang Sengbian at Baling but could not overcome him and returned defeated; he then killed Quan at Jiangxia and cast his corpse into the Huanghe Ford.
units.literal: Later Jing attacked Wang Sengbian at Baling but could not overcome him and returned defeated; he then killed Quan at Jiangxia and cast his corpse into the Huanghe Ford.

units.zh: 初，泉之爲南討都督也，其友人夢泉得罪于世祖，覺而告之。
units.en: Earlier, when Quan was commander-in-chief of the southern campaign, a friend dreamed that Quan had offended Emperor Yuan; on waking he told him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Quan was commander-in-chief of the southern campaign, a friend dreamed that Quan had offended Shizu; on waking he told him.

units.zh: 後未旬，果見囚執。
units.en: Within less than ten days afterward, he was indeed imprisoned.
units.literal: Within less than ten days afterward, he was indeed seen imprisoned.

units.zh: 頃之，又夢泉著朱衣而行水上，又告泉曰：「君勿憂，尋得免矣。」
units.en: Before long he again dreamed that Quan wore red robes and walked upon the water, and again told Quan, "Do not worry — you will soon be released."
units.literal: Before long he again dreamed that Quan wore red robes and walked upon the water, and again told Quan, "Do not worry — you will soon be released."

units.zh: 因說其夢，泉密記之，俄而復見任，皆如其夢。
units.en: He then related the dream; Quan secretly recorded it, and soon afterward was again employed — all as in the dream.
units.literal: He then related the dream; Quan secretly recorded it, and soon afterward was again employed — all as in the dream.

units.zh: 泉於《儀禮》尤明，撰《新儀》四十卷，行於世。
units.en: Quan was especially expert in the Ceremonies and composed New Ceremonies in forty juan, which circulated in his day.
units.literal: Quan was especially clear in the Ceremonies and composed New Ceremonies in forty juan, circulating in the world.

units.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：阮孝緒常言，仲尼論四科，始乎德行，終乎文學。
units.en: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: Ruan Xiaoxu often said that in Confucius's discussion of the four categories, he began with virtue and conduct and ended with letters and learning.
units.literal: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: Ruan Xiaoxu often said that in Confucius's discussion of the four categories, he began with virtue and conduct and ended with letters and learning.

units.zh: 有行者多尚質樸，有文者少蹈規矩，故衛、石靡餘論可傳，屈、賈無立德之譽。
units.en: Those with conduct mostly esteem plain simplicity; those with letters seldom tread within rules. Therefore Wei and Shi have no remaining discourse worth handing down, while Qu Yuan and Jia Yi have no reputation for establishing virtue.
units.literal: Those with conduct mostly esteem plain simplicity; those with letters seldom tread within rules. Therefore Wei and Shi have no remaining discourse worth handing down, while Qu and Jia have no reputation for establishing virtue.

units.zh: 若夫憲章游、夏，祖述回、騫，體兼文行，於裴幾原見之矣。
units.en: In modeling oneself on Ziyou and Zixia, following in the footsteps of Yan Hui and Min Ziqian, and combining literary talent with moral conduct — all of this we see in Pei Jiyuan.
units.literal: As for taking You and Xia as models, tracing back to Yan and Qian, embodying both letters and conduct — in Pei Jiyuan we have seen it.

units.zh: 太宗簡文皇帝諱綱，字世纘，小字六通，高祖第三子，昭明太子母弟也。
units.en: Taizong Emperor Jianwen, personal name Gang, courtesy name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong, was Gaozu's third son and Zhaoming Crown Prince's younger brother by the same mother.
units.literal: The Taizong Emperor Jianwen was tabooed Gang, style name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong; he was the third son of the Gaozu and a uterine younger brother of Crown Prince Zhaoming.

units.zh: 初，太宗見幽縶，題壁自序云：「有梁正士蘭陵蕭世纘，立身行道，終始如一，風雨如晦，雞鳴不已。
units.en: At first, when Taizong was held captive, he wrote on the wall: "I, Xiao Shizuan of Lanling, upright man of Liang, one in conduct from start to finish—though wind and rain darken the sky, the cock crows without cease.
units.literal: At first, when Taizong was imprisoned, he wrote a self-account on the wall, saying: "I, Xiao Shizuan of Lanling, upright man of Liang, in conduct from first to last one—though wind and rain darken the sky, the cock crows without cease.

units.zh: 晉安王綱，文義生知，孝敬自然，威惠外宣，德行內敏，羣后歸美，率土宅心。
units.en: Prince Gang of Jin'an was gifted in letters and principles, naturally filial and respectful, his authority and kindness known abroad and his virtue keen within; the lords praised him and the realm took him to heart.
units.literal: Prince of Jin'an Gang, gifted in letters and right by nature, filial and respectful by instinct, his authority and kindness proclaimed abroad and virtue and conduct keen within, the feudal lords admired him and all the land took him to heart.

units.zh: 明年，三月己丑，王僧辯率前百官奉梓宮升朝堂，世祖追崇為簡文皇帝，廟曰太宗。
units.en: The next year, on jichou in the third month, Wang Senbian led the former hundred officials to raise the coffin to the audience hall; Shizu posthumously honored him as Emperor Jianwen with temple name Taizong.
units.literal: The next year, third month, day jichou, Wang Senbian led the former hundred officials in escorting the coffin up the audience hall; Shizu posthumously honored him as Emperor Jianwen, with temple name Taizong.

units.zh: 五年，封晉安王，食邑八千戶。
units.en: In year 5 he was made Prince of Jin'an with a fief of eight thousand households.
units.literal: In year 5 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an with a fief of eight thousand households.

units.zh: 戊午，侯景遣衛尉卿彭俊、廂公王僧貴率兵入殿，廢太宗為晉安王，幽于永福省。
units.en: On wuwu day Hou Jing sent minister of the guard Peng Jun and palace section commander Wang Senggui with troops into the hall, deposed Taizong as Prince of Jin'an, and imprisoned him in Yongfu Palace.
units.literal: On wuwu, Hou Jing sent Minister of the Guard Peng Jun and Palace Section Commander Wang Senggui to lead troops into the hall, deposed Taizong as Prince of Jin'an, and confined him in Yongfu Palace.

units.zh: 可立為皇太子。」
units.en: He is to be established as crown prince."
units.literal: He may be established as crown prince."

units.zh: 賊偽諡曰明皇帝，廟稱高宗。
units.en: The rebels gave him the posthumous title Bright Emperor and the temple name Gaozong.
units.literal: The rebels gave the posthumous title Bright Emperor and the temple name Gaozong.

units.zh: 辛巳，卽皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi he took the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi he ascended the imperial throne.

units.zh: 雅好題詩，其序云：「余七歲有詩癖，長而不倦。」
units.en: He loved poetry by nature; in his preface he wrote, "At seven I had a poetry mania, and as I grew I never tired of it."
units.literal: He loved composing poetry by nature; in his preface he wrote: "At seven I had a poetry mania, and in growing up I never tired of it."

units.zh: 然傷於輕豔，當時號曰「宮體」。
units.en: Yet he was faulted for frivolous ornament, and his age called it the "Palace Style."
units.literal: Yet he was faulted for frivolous ornament, and his age styled this the "Palace Style."

units.zh: 所著《昭明太子傳》五卷，《諸王傳》三十卷，《禮大義》二十卷，《老子義》二十卷，《莊子義》二十卷，《長春義記》一百卷，《法寶連璧》三百卷，並行於世焉。
units.en: His works included Biography of the Heir Apparent Zhaoming in five scrolls, Biographies of the Princes in thirty scrolls, Great Meaning of the Rites in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Laozi in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Zhuangzi in twenty scrolls, Recorded Meaning of Eternal Spring in one hundred scrolls, and Treasured Laws Linked Pearls in three hundred scrolls—all circulated in his day.
units.literal: His works included Biography of the Heir Apparent Zhaoming in five scrolls, Biographies of the Princes in thirty scrolls, Great Meaning of the Rites in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Laozi in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Zhuangzi in twenty scrolls, Recorded Meaning of Eternal Spring in one hundred scrolls, and Treasured Laws Linked Pearls in three hundred scrolls—all circulated in his time.

units.zh: 博綜儒書，善言玄理。
units.en: He mastered Confucian classics and was skilled in Neo-Daoist discourse.
units.literal: Broadly versed in Confucian books, skilled in discoursing on Dark Learning.

units.zh: 高祖所制《五經講疏》，嘗於玄圃奉述，聽者傾朝野。
units.en: When Gaozu composed his Expositions on the Five Classics, Taizong once lectured on them at the Dark Garden; listeners filled court and countryside.
units.literal: When Gaozu composed Expositions on the Five Classics, Taizong once presented them at the Dark Garden; listeners filled court and countryside.

units.zh: 是歲，丁所生穆貴嬪喪，上表陳解，詔還攝本任。
units.en: That year, when his birth mother Honored Consort Mu died, he asked to resign but was ordered back to his post.
units.literal: That year, on mourning for his birth mother Honored Consort Mu, he submitted a memorial requesting release; an edict ordered him to resume his original duties.

units.zh: 天監二年十月丁未，生於顯陽殿。
units.en: On dingwei in the tenth month of Tianjian 2 he was born in Xianyang Hall.
units.literal: In the tenth month, day dingwei, year 2 of Tianjian, he was born in Xianyang Hall.

units.zh: 旣醉寢，王偉、彭儁進土囊，王修纂坐其上，於是太宗崩於永福省，時年四十九。
units.en: When he was drunk and asleep, Wang Wei and Peng Jun brought in a bag of earth; Wang Xiuzuan sat on it—and Taizong died in Yongfu Palace at the age of forty-nine.
units.literal: When he was drunk and asleep, Wang Wei and Peng Jun brought in a bag of earth; Wang Xiuzuan sat upon it—and thereupon Taizong died in Yongfu Palace, aged forty-nine.

units.zh: 太清三年五月丙辰，高祖崩。
units.en: On bingchen in the fifth month of Taiqing 3 Gaozu died.
units.literal: In the fifth month, day bingchen, year 3 of Taiqing, the Gaozu died.

units.zh: 八年，為雲麾將軍，領石頭戍軍事，量置佐吏。
units.en: In year 8 he became General of the Cloud Banner, took charge of Shitou garrison affairs, and had aides appointed as required.
units.literal: In year 8 he was made General of the Cloud Banner, supervising military affairs at the Shitou garrison, with assistant officials appointed as needed.

units.zh: 九年，遷使持節、都督南北兗青徐冀五州諸軍事、宣毅將軍、南兗州刺史。
units.en: In year 9 he was made Bearer of the Staff and commander of the five Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji provinces, General Who Proclaims Resolution, and South Yanzhou inspector.
units.literal: In year 9 he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the five provinces North and South Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji, made General Who Proclaims Resolution and South Yanzhou Inspector.

units.zh: 十二年，入為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹。
units.en: In year 12 he entered court as General Who Proclaims Grace and intendant of Danyang.
units.literal: In year 12 he entered the capital as General Who Proclaims Grace and Intendant of Danyang.

units.zh: 十三年，出為使持節、都督荊雍梁南北秦益寧七州諸軍事、南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，將軍如故。
units.en: In year 13 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Jing, Yong, Liang, the two Qin, Yi, and Ning, Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, and Jingzhou inspector, retaining his generalship.
units.literal: In year 13 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces Jing, Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Yi, and Ning, made Colonel of the Southern Barbarians and Jingzhou Inspector, his generalship unchanged.

units.zh: 十四年，徙為都督江州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、江州刺史，持節如故。
units.en: In year 14 he was reassigned commander of Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Banner, and Jiangzhou inspector, still Bearer of the Staff.
units.literal: In year 14 he was reassigned as Commander over military affairs in Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Banner and Jiangzhou Inspector, Bearer of the Staff unchanged.

units.zh: 十七年，徵為西中郎將、領石頭戍軍事，尋復為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹，加侍中。
units.en: In year 17 he was recalled as Leader of the Palace Gentlemen of the West with Shitou garrison duties, then again General Who Proclaims Grace and Danyang intendant, with Palace Attendant added.
units.literal: In year 17 he was summoned as Leader of the Palace Gentlemen of the West, supervising the Shitou garrison; soon restored as General Who Proclaims Grace and Intendant of Danyang, additionally made Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 未拜，改授雲麾將軍、南徐州刺史。
units.en: before taking office he was reassigned General of the Cloud Banner and South Xuzhou inspector.
units.literal: before assuming the post, he was reassigned as General of the Cloud Banner and South Xuzhou Inspector.

units.zh: 四年，徙為使持節、都督雍梁、南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事，平西將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
units.en: In year 4 he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yong, Liang, the two Qin, and related districts, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of Pacified Barbarians, and Yongzhou inspector.
units.literal: In year 4 he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in Yong and Liang, North and South Qin, the four provinces, Jingzhou's Jingling, and Sizhou's Su commandery, made General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of Pacified Barbarians, and Yongzhou Inspector.

units.zh: 五年，進號安北將軍。
units.en: In year 5 he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.
units.literal: In year 5 he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.

units.zh: 二年，徵為都督南揚、徐二州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、揚州刺史。
units.en: In year 2 he was recalled as commander of South Yang and Xu, General of Agile Cavalry, and Yangzhou inspector.
units.literal: In year 2 he was summoned as Commander over military affairs in South Yang and Xu, made General of Agile Cavalry and Yangzhou Inspector.

units.zh: 七月乙亥，臨軒策拜，以脩繕東宮，權居東府。
units.en: On yihai in the seventh month he was invested at the throne hall; while the Eastern Palace was repaired he lodged temporarily at the Eastern Mansion.
units.literal: On yihai in the seventh month, the enthronement ceremony was held at the imperial hall; because the Eastern Palace was under repair, he temporarily resided at the Eastern Mansion.

units.zh: 普通元年，出為使持節、都督益寧雍梁南北秦沙七州諸軍事、益州刺史；
